instruction: Locate and access the Google Scholar page of the contact author using Chrome browser.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-40)

metadata.explanation: Paraphrase using 'Locate and access' action sequence and 'contact author' terminology. The contact/correspondence author is Tianlin (Tim) Shi, as indicated in the PDF footer 'Correspondence to: Tianlin (Tim) Shi <tianlin@cs.stanford.edu>'. His Google Scholar profile user ID is qRAQ5BsAAAAJ. Task requires: (1) finding the contact author information in the PDF, (2) searching for the author on Google Scholar, (3) opening their citations page. Evaluator uses existing is_expected_url_pattern_match metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts active Chrome tab URL from accessibility tree
Metric correctly verifies URL contains both Google Scholar citations base URL and specific author user ID
Expected values are semantically correct: Google Scholar citations URL and Tianlin (Tim) Shi's user ID (qRAQ5BsAAAAJ)
Complete coverage: evaluator verifies the core requirement - accessing the specific author's Google Scholar page
Logical flow is sound: getter extracts URL → metric checks both required patterns → returns 1.0 if both match
No postconfig needed: accessibility tree persists with loaded page, getter can read URL after navigation
